records.rationale: Both descriptions ("Supply id") purely restate the key name without naming a specific entity; the adapter rules only describe URL-macro transmission mechanics ('substituted into the endpoint URL as a macro') without stating what entity 'supply' refers to, so identifier's naming bar is not met and no other role fits.

records.name: tagId
records.rationale: Multiple descriptions name the referenced entity (ad tag / tag ID); the nexx360 adapter rule about the tag_id query parameter is consistent transmission detail.
records.quote: An ID which identifies the deepintent ad tag

records.name: tag_id
records.rationale: Explicitly names the referenced entity, an ad placement.
records.quote: Identifies specific ad placement.

records.name: tagid
records.rationale: Descriptions consistently name referenced entities (inventory target, placement ID); the validation rules (must parse as non-zero integer) are format constraints, not conflicting semantics.
records.quote: The id of an inventory target

records.name: tappxkey
records.rationale: Despite the '-key' suffix in the name, the only source text explicitly says it identifies an adunit entity rather than authenticating anything; the required-field adapter rule is consistent transmission/validation detail.
records.quote: An ID which identifies the adunit

records.name: targeting
records.rationale: Direct match to the targeting role; the adnuntius adapter rule describing relocation of category/segments/keywords/keyValues sub-fields reinforces audience/content targeting semantics.
records.quote: Targeting information in key value pairs

records.name: targets
records.rationale: "Target params, as defined in your Adhese setup" adds no concrete semantics beyond the name itself — it does not say whether these are audience/content targeting values, slot configuration, or something else.

records.name: tenantId
records.rationale: Explicitly names the referenced entity, a tenant; the adapter rule about the pid query parameter is transmission detail only.
records.quote: Synapse HX tenant identifier

records.name: test
records.rationale: Multiple descriptions (test-creatives flag, testing-only flag, 'TestMode', 'Switch that enables test responses') describe exactly the test-flag example given in delivery-control's definition.
records.quote: Switch that enables test responses

records.name: tid
records.rationale: Both descriptions explicitly name the referenced entity, a placement.
records.quote: Placement ID

records.name: token
records.rationale: pass1 skeptic: The chosen quote (smarthub: fills a 'SourceId' macro) does support identifier, but alkimi's description 'Publisher Token provided by Alkimi' reads as a platform-issued authentication token, and bluesea's rejection message pairs it with 'pubid' ('empty pubid or token') in a way that is equally consistent with a credential required alongside an identifier. The role vocabulary itself lists 'token' as the canonical credential example. Different bidders plausibly use this shared field name for different purposes (identifier for smarthub, credential for alkimi), so a single role cannot be established with confidence from this evidence.

records.name: tokenId
records.rationale: The single description ('Token ID') purely restates the key name; no adapter rule evidence exists.

records.name: track
records.rationale: "Id of a forced Track" is too vague to establish which entity or behavior 'Track' refers to; no adapter rule evidence.

records.name: trafficSourceCode
records.rationale: Both descriptions only state the field is deprecated in favor of traffic_source_code, without describing what the field itself represents.

records.name: traffic_source_code
records.rationale: Names the referenced entity, the third-party traffic source, consistently across three bidder descriptions.
records.quote: Specifies the third-party source of this impression.

records.name: ttx
records.rationale: The key 'ttx' itself carries no description; the only evidence available (zoneid defaulting from siteId, and an injected caller name/version object) describes behavior of its sub-fields (ext.ttx.zoneid, ext.ttx.caller), not of the 'ttx' container key itself.

records.name: type
records.rationale: pass1 skeptic: The delivery-control quote is well-corroborated (four independently verified adapters injecting the same publisher/network discriminator), but the sole schema description for this name, adquery's 'Bid type', is a distinct piece of evidence from an unrelated bidder and in RTB terminology 'bid type' commonly denotes the ad/media format of a bid (banner/video/native), directly matching format-declaration's definition. With 18 total adapter rules and only 4 sampled, the field name is used across many independent bidder contexts and 'Bid type' shows at least one of them plausibly means something else entirely.

records.name: uid
records.rationale: All four descriptions name a referenced entity (ad unit / placement / ad slot); the grid required-by-adapter drop-if-absent rule is consistent enforcement, not conflicting semantics.
records.quote: An ID which identifies this placement of the impression

records.name: unit
records.rationale: Both descriptions name a specific referenced entity (inventory target / ad unit).
records.quote: The ad unit id.

records.name: unitId
records.rationale: Both descriptions ('The unit ID from Consumable', 'Unit ID') merely restate the key name without naming a more specific entity than the bare name itself.

records.name: unitName
records.rationale: "Expected to be a valid CSS class name" describes a display/styling detail that does not clearly map to any of the ten closed roles (not an opaque identifier reference, not a defined media capability/constraint); no adapter rule evidence to clarify further.

records.name: us_privacy
records.rationale: Adapter-rule behaviour text explicitly names a 'US privacy string' (CCPA) whose presence/value gates the request — a privacy-consent signal, not merely a name echo.
records.quote: Any non-empty US privacy string rejects the entire request.

records.name: useSourceBidderCode
records.rationale: A boolean switch that changes which bidder code is reported in bid responses — a behavioural mode flag, matching delivery-control's 'mode' category.
records.quote: Use the bidder code of the actual server-side bidder in bid responses

records.name: use_payment_rule
records.rationale: Boolean signalling application of a payment/revenue rule; corroborated by the sibling use_pmt_rule evidence tying the same concept explicitly to net price — a pricing/payment-rule switch, not a generic control.
records.quote: apply the relevant payment rule

records.name: use_pmt_rule
records.rationale: msft's description explicitly ties the flag to 'net price' calculation from publisher payment rules — a monetary/pricing behaviour, matching the pricing role (revenue share/bid adjustment family).
records.quote: return net price after publisher payment rules are applied

records.name: userKey
records.rationale: Text names the referenced entity (user) directly ('user key'); the remainder of the sentence describes consent-gating conditions on its USE, not what the field itself represents, so identifier — not privacy-consent — is the correct role.
records.quote: publisher-supplied user key

records.name: version
records.rationale: Injected value is explicitly a software version stamp — descriptive integration context that controls nothing, textbook metadata.
records.quote: Stamped with the running prebid-server version.

records.name: video
records.rationale: Rubicon's description ('additional Rubicon video parameters') only restates the key name with no concrete capability, constraint, or behaviour disclosed — same failure mode as the PID/PId example; no role is established.

records.name: videoResponseType
records.rationale: Description explains the field selects/declares which ad response markup format is returned (VAST vs VPAID, mp4/webm media files) — the field declares the ad format itself.
records.quote: the video response will be an AdM element containing VAST 3.0 markup

records.name: videotype
records.rationale: Adapter injects a value selecting the rewarded-ad subtype/format on the video object — directly declares the ad format.
records.quote: "rewarded_interstitial" when instl is 1, otherwise "rewarded"

records.name: viewabilityPercentage
records.rationale: pass1 skeptic: Quote is verbatim, but the field is a value declared by the supply side as part of the outbound BID REQUEST describing an inherent characteristic of the ad slot (like sizes or position-on-page), not an observed value reported back after the fact. Measurement's own definition specifies 'reports rather than controls,' but a request-time declared characteristic used to inform bid decisions fits media-property (a slot/placement characteristic) at least as well.

records.name: visitor
records.rationale: Description uses the word 'targeting' explicitly and ties the key/value pairs to the visitor — a direct match for the targeting role.
records.quote: targeting key/value pairs related to the visitor

records.name: vungle
records.rationale: pass1 skeptic: The quoted phrase is verbatim (from the adapterRule detail: 'A "vungle" object holding placement_reference_id, app_store_id and bid_token is added to imp.ext...'), but it names the CHILD fields living inside the vungle object, not the vungle field itself. There is zero description or rule text characterizing what 'vungle' (the ext namespace key) itself references — its role is inferred by imputing the children's identifier-ness upward onto the parent container, which is structural/lexical inference, not direct evidence. A field literally named after the bidder (Vungle) used purely as an ext namespace key is at least as plausible under 'metadata' (vocabulary's own example: 'partner/vendor name') as under 'identifier'. Both adapterRule entries are also marked status:unverified, weakening the evidentiary basis further.

records.name: website
records.rationale: Explicitly labelled an identifier and names the referenced entity (the publisher's website/site).
records.quote: Publisher website identifier

records.name: wid
records.rationale: theadx's description names the referenced entity (inventory source) explicitly; gamma's thinner 'Web ID' is consistent with the same identifier role, not conflicting.
records.quote: An ID which identifies the Theadx inventory source id

records.name: widgetId
records.rationale: Names the referenced entity (this Nativery widget, an ad-unit-like entity) explicitly, satisfying the identifier bar.
records.quote: An ID which identifies this Nativery widget

records.name: wrapper
records.rationale: 'Specifies pubmatic openwrap configuration for a publisher' is generic ('configuration') with no disclosed switch, limit, timeout, or controlled behaviour — the biddercode sub-field detail belongs to a distinct nested path, not to 'wrapper' itself; no role is cleanly established without stretching.

records.name: zid
records.rationale: Description expands the abbreviation to name a concrete referenced entity from the enumerated list (zone), unlike a circular restatement (e.g. 'PID' for 'PId'); reinforced by the adapter rule requiring the value be non-empty.
records.quote: Zone ID

records.name: zone
records.rationale: Multiple bidder descriptions consistently name the referenced entity (zone) explicitly; no conflicting role is suggested by any of the quoted text.
records.quote: An ID which identifies the zone selling the impression

records.name: zoneId
records.rationale: Descriptions across bidders name different specific entities (zone vs publisher) but all are identifier-class references; entity disagreement across vendors is not role-level ambiguity since both fall under the same closed role.
records.quote: Publisher Id to use.

records.name: zoneIds
records.rationale: No descriptions and no adapter rules at all (zero total evidence) — nothing to quote, so no role can be established.

records.name: zone_id
records.rationale: Explicitly labelled an identifier naming the referenced entity (ad zone); corroborated by smartrtb/sovrnXsp describing it as a zone ID for a placement belonging to app/site.
records.quote: The ad zone identifier

records.name: zoneid
records.rationale: Criteo's description explicitly names the referenced entity (zone, tied to the impression); silvermob's matching 'Zone ID' and the adapter rule (substituted into the endpoint URL) are consistent with the same identifier role.
records.quote: Impression's zone ID.
